verdicts.strongest_argument: The verdict is published inside the admissible corpus by two separate publishers and the bars show the market absorbing it and going up. The finding's own source (docs/893b8caad61d5614d48335b85cebe444a3c36817.txt, from admissible snapshot 20260830T152925Z) is a dated 2026-08-04 page that carries every number in the claim -- the $88m split $77m/$11m, no punitives, no fraud, the ~2,400 federal MDL / ~7,450 Massachusetts / Minnesota coordinated action counts, and the 'no global settlement' framing. So the case-count leg the hunter treats as the size of the tail is in the same public document as the headline, not one step beyond it. Independently, the Star Tribune story on the same federal bellwether appears twice in the capture: as a URL in snapshot 20260830T152925Z's skipped list, and as a link posted to the $MDT Stocktwits feed on 2026-08-09 (docs/dd07807b1a0282e03d16c9e4a92a1ce97869b713.txt, fetched 2026-08-30T08:36:22Z from admissible snapshot 20260830T083620Z). That is a metro daily in the company's home market plus retail circulation, three weeks before the print. The tape then says what the market did with it: 2026-08-03 close 86.68 -> 08-04 (verdict day) 86.20, -0.55% on 6.36m shares against a 6.84m 20d average, i.e. a nothing day; 08-07 +1.44% and 08-10 +2.58%; and by 08-19 the stock was 94.13, +9.2% from the verdict close. The information was out and the stock rose through it. Arithmetic supports that being rational rather than an oversight: $88m is 0.076% of the $115.16bn market cap in event.json, and even a full-docket provision at Bard-like per-claim economics across ~9,850 cases is under 1% of cap, arriving as a 10-Q contingency footnote rather than in an FQ1 P&L. What the corpus genuinely does not contain is any sell-side or preview note sizing the aggregate, which is why this is not a 90.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This one is in the captured trade press under a headline that is the claim, and it is in the price bars on the day it became public. MedTech Dive published 'Medtronic recalls pH monitoring capsule linked to 184 serious injuries' on 2026-08-28 (docs/2edb580f0dd2d292f6dec88e4ab4151efd4c407e.txt: schema datePublished 2026-08-28T12:56:00, byline 'Published Aug. 28, 2026', body 'As of Aug. 10, Medtronic had received reports of 184 serious injuries and no deaths'), and it is item sha 2edb580f in the admissible snapshot 20260830T152925Z. The primary FDA page in the same snapshot carries its own dates: schema datePublished 'Thu, 08/27/2026' and 'Content current as of: 08/27/2026'. So the hunter's source_date of 2026-08-10 is the injury-count as-of date, not the publication date -- the alert went public on 2026-08-27, five sessions before the print, not three and a half weeks. On that exact date the stock fell 92.02 -> 89.97, -2.23% on 7.77m shares against a 6.84m 20d average, the largest single down day in the whole admissible window and about 1.7x a one-day move at the baseline's 21.3% realised vol. I state that as consistency rather than proof of causation, but the date match is exact and it is the only candidate news on the tape. The Harmony leg is published in the corpus too: its own FDA page (sha a866ba69) and MedTech Dive 825186 'Medtronic recalls heart valve delivery catheter for risk of tip detaching' are both admissible items in the same snapshot. On size the finding concedes the point -- Bravo is immaterial to revenue against a $115bn cap -- so the residual is a product-liability seed that cannot land in an FQ1 print. Not 95 only because no sell-side note in the admissible corpus connects the alert to the quarter's numbers.
